title: Cost-Quality-Latency Triage Matrix (working notes)
body:
Purpose:
This working sheet describes a compact SLO-driven triage matrix that maps per-query latency/quality/cost constraints to a recommended quantization tier (INT8 / FP8 / 4-bit). The intent is not to replace per-model evals, but to give a lightweight, repeatable spreadsheet that product and infra teams can use to quickly categorize workloads and surface plausible default recommendations for experimentation.

Audience:
- Product managers evaluating cost vs SLA tradeoffs
- Infra and runtime engineers sizing Dedicated pools and autoscale policies
- ML engineers deciding which quant modes to benchmark first for a workload

High-level idea:
1) Normalize the three axes (cost, latency, quality) to a common [0..1] penalty scale where 0 = no penalty (ideal) and 1 = maximum observed penalty across candidate quant modes.
2) Combine via a weighted triage score: triage = w_cost * cost_penalty + w_latency * latency_penalty + w_quality * quality_penalty. Lower triage = better fit for aggressive quant (e.g., 4-bit).
3) Map triage ranges to actions: 
   - triage <= 0.25 -> "Recommend: aggressive (4-bit) trial with narrow prompt tests"
   - 0.25 < triage <= 0.55 -> "Recommend: mid (INT8 or FP8) with evaluation set"
   - triage > 0.55 -> "Recommend: conservative (FP32/FP16) or INT8 only after targeted evals"

Spreadsheet layout (columns):
- workload_id (string)
- sla_latency_ms (number) -- SLO per-request p50 or p95 latency threshold (ms)
- baseline_cost_per_1k_tokens (USD)
- baseline_latency_ms (ms)
- baseline_quality (0..1) -- e.g., surrogate metric (BLEU/ROUGE/QA-accuracy/training eval)
- variant (FP32 / INT8 / FP8 / 4bit)
- variant_cost_per_1k_tokens (USD)
- variant_latency_ms (ms)
- variant_quality (0..1)
- cost_reduction_pct = (baseline_cost - variant_cost) / baseline_cost
- latency_improvement_pct = (baseline_latency - variant_latency) / baseline_latency
- quality_drop_pct = (baseline_quality - variant_quality) / baseline_quality
- normalized_cost_penalty = 1 - cost_reduction_pct_norm (see notes)
- normalized_latency_penalty = IF(variant_latency_ms <= sla_latency_ms, 0, normalized_overrun)
- normalized_quality_penalty = quality_drop_pct_norm
- triage_score = w_cost*normalized_cost_penalty + w_latency*normalized_latency_penalty + w_quality*normalized_quality_penalty
- recommendation (text)

Normalization approach (one plausible method):
- For cost: compute candidate cost_reduction_pct across variants; set max_reduction = MAX(cost_reduction_pct); cost_penalty = 1 - (cost_reduction_pct / max_reduction). That yields 0 for the variant that reduces cost most, 1 for the variant that gives no reduction. (Alternative: clamp to [0,1] by design.)
- For latency: treat any variant that meets the SLO as 0 penalty. For variants exceeding SLO, convert overrun_ms to penalty by dividing by worst_overrun across all variants and capping at 1.
- For quality: quality_drop_pct normalized by the largest observed drop. We treat larger drops as higher penalty. If variant_quality > baseline_quality (rare), set penalty=0.

Triage weights (start points; tune per product):
- w_cost = 0.5 (cost-first workloads)
- w_latency = 0.3
- w_quality = 0.2
Note: for latency-sensitive product buckets we flip weights to w_latency=0.5, w_cost=0.3, w_quality=0.2. For safety/regulatory impacts, quality weight should be >= 0.5.

Worked example (single workload):
- workload_id: search-snippet-gen
- sla_latency_ms: 100 (p95)
- baseline (FP32): baseline_cost_per_1k_tokens = $0.12, baseline_latency_ms = 120, baseline_quality = 0.95
- INT8: variant_cost = $0.06, variant_latency = 95, variant_quality = 0.942
- FP8: variant_cost = $0.05, variant_latency = 100, variant_quality = 0.935
- 4-bit: variant_cost = $0.035, variant_latency = 88, variant_quality = 0.88

Compute intermediates (manual numbers):
- cost_reduction_pct: INT8 = 50%, FP8 = 58.3%, 4bit = 70.8% (baseline reduction = (0.12 - v)/0.12)
- max_reduction = 70.8% -> normalized cost penalties: INT8 = 1 - (0.5 / 0.708) = 0.293, FP8 = 1 - (0.583 / 0.708) = 0.177, 4bit = 0 (best cost)
- latency penalty: baseline p95 is 120ms but SLO = 100ms; we treat meeting SLO as 0. INT8 latency 95ms -> 0, FP8 100ms -> 0 (equal to SLO), 4bit 88ms -> 0
- quality_drop_pct: INT8 = (0.95 - 0.942)/0.95 = 0.0084 (0.84%), FP8 = 0.0158 (1.58%), 4bit = 0.0737 (7.37%)
- max_quality_drop = 7.37% -> normalized quality penalties: INT8 = 0.0084/0.0737 = 0.114, FP8 = 0.215, 4bit = 1.0

Apply weights (cost-first): w_cost=0.5, w_latency=0.3, w_quality=0.2
- INT8 triage = 0.5*0.293 + 0.3*0 + 0.2*0.114 = 0.1465 + 0 + 0.0228 = 0.1693 -> Recommend: INT8 trial (low triage)
- FP8 triage = 0.5*0.177 + 0.3*0 + 0.2*0.215 = 0.0885 + 0 + 0.043 = 0.1315 -> Recommend: FP8 (even lower triage)
- 4bit triage = 0.5*0 + 0.3*0 + 0.2*1.0 = 0 + 0 + 0.2 = 0.2 -> Recommend: 4-bit trial but with strict quality eval (triage near 0.25 boundary)

Interpretation: for this workload (SLO=100ms and cost-sensitive), FP8 and INT8 both look attractive; 4-bit offers big cost upside but introduces a significant quality penalty that requires focused evals. The spreadsheet surfaces that nuance clearly even though raw cost numbers alone would have pushed to 4-bit.

Decision guideline snippets (to capture in final playbook):
- If triage < 0.15: schedule automated A/B eval on 1k representative prompts, consider canary rollout to 5% traffic for 48–72 hours.
- If 0.15 <= triage <= 0.35: do an offline eval on 5–10k prompts, add qualitative human review on top 200 edge cases, block 4-bit canary unless pass quality gates.
- If triage > 0.35: avoid aggressive quantization in production; consider caching/ batching knobs instead or model distillation strategies.

Operational checklist (what to run on shortlist variant):
- Per-variant latency microbench at target batch sizes and sequence lengths (p50/p95)
- Token-cost simulation for expected traffic distribution (include prefix caching savings)
- End-to-end functional eval: 5k prompts relevant to product slice + 200 edge cases
- Human-in-the-loop spot checks and hallucination/error triage
- Keymetrics: delta in cost per 1M tokens, p95 latency change, failure/hallucination rate delta, user-facing KPI delta (CTR/retention) if available

Caveats & open questions:
- Quality metric selection: a single numeric quality_score may hide distributional failures — include per-intent or per-prompt buckets where possible.
- Some quant modes vary by model architecture (LLaMA-like vs Mistral). Baseline numbers must be model+compilation-specific.
- Thresholds and weights should be tuned per product line and historically validated with canaries.
- This sheet assumes costs reported per-1k tokens; non-linear pricing (commits, reserved instance amortization) should be folded into a monthly TCO view for Dedicated customers.

Next steps (owner: Aisha):
- Convert these working notes into a live Google Sheet with formula cells matching the layout above (deadline: 2024-11-12).
- Push a tiny automation that pulls bench CSVs from nightly perf job into the sheet (Jamal).
- Run a 2-week experiment on search-snippet-gen variants (Marcus) and collect the three core metrics for finalizing weight recommendations.

Notes to reviewers: please look for: 1) realism of example numbers, 2) a useful default for weights, 3) whether SLO handling (zero penalty if meet SLO) feels too permissive.
